text:
alex: Morning — proposing a change to our perf CI: capture full nsys traces + perfetto timelines for both PR gates and a nightly profiling sweep. Goal: root-cause kernel selection regressions, batching hotspots, and KV cache warmup behavior.

maya: 👍 agree. quick q — how big are the artifacts going to be? nsys files blow up.

alex: Typical nsys for a 10s workload is ~100-400MB compressed depending on surface area. Plan: PR gate = lightweight snapshot (3s) + kernel summary; nightly = full nsys + perfetto. Upload to s3 with lifecycle policy (30d) and optional transition to IA after 7d.

liam: Can we be smarter: sample short snapshots on every PR, then run a full parametrized sweep nightly (different batch sizes/seq-len/model variants)? Also ensure symbol tables for custom kernels get uploaded.

alex: Yep. Proposed jobs: perf-pr-snapshot, perf-nightly-sweep. PR job does minimal capture and runs trace-summarizer. Nightly runs kernel-sweep list and emits raw traces + summaries. Example PR snippet: 
```
jobs:
  perf-pr-snapshot:
    runs-on: gpu
    steps:
      - run: nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --output=pr-${{ github.sha }} --duration=3s ./ci/run_perf --scenario=kv-warmup
      - run: python tools/ci/upload_traces.py pr-${{ github.sha }}.nsys s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/pr/
```

sophia: upload_traces should gzip, attach metadata.json with git_sha/model/seq_len/batch_size/kernel_config. Also tag whether run used quantized kernels so diffs are comparable.

alex: agreed — metadata will include: git_sha, branch, model, seq_len, batch_size, quant_mode, kv_cold_start (bool), runner_id. For nightly we do: 
```
nsys profile -o nightly-${date} --stats=true ./ci/run_perf --scenario=kernel-sweep --seq-len=2048
perfetto --out=nightly-${date}.pftrace --record
```

perf-ci-bot: job perf-pr-snapshot started on runner gpu-14

maya: How will diffs be computed? Dashboard needs per-kernel timelines and p50/p95/p99.

liam: We'll run trace-quant (our trace analysis) to produce JSON summaries: {kernel_name -> {hist, total_time_ms, calls}} and a separate kv_metrics.json with hit_rate and cold_start_count. Diff job compares latest nightly JSON vs baseline and flags >5% regression in total_time or >10% increase in cold-start.

sophia: Also flag if kernel variant switches under the same model/seq_len — that's often an autotune behavior that hides regressions. We should map kernel variants to families and compare at family-level when necessary.

alex: Good point. We'll maintain a kernel_family_map file in repo that maps variant names to families and a fallback strategy (family-compare or strict). Diff job will annotate whether a change was a variant swap.

maya: Ownership/costs? Finance asked about storage.

zach: infra will shard uploads and apply lifecycle rules. Estimate: with current test matrix we expect ~30-50GB/day for nightly raw + PR snapshots; S3 standard ~$25-40/mo. Can transition to IA after 3-7d to cut cost. We'll also dedupe identical traces (sha-based) before upload.

alex: I'll draft the GH Actions + upload script PR. Target: EOW for merge. Volunteers for review + smoke on staging: @maya @liam @sophia?

maya: I'll run the smoke tomorrow.

liam: I'll validate the trace-quant summaries and diff thresholds.

perf-ci-bot: perf-pr-snapshot succeeded (3s) — uploaded pr-abcdef.nsys.gz to s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/pr/ — size 142MB

alex: Thanks — next step: build a small dashboard that shows per-kernel delta, call counts, and KV hit-rate trend; surface alerts for regressions. We should also surface the top-5 hotspots and a link to full perfetto timeline.

sophia: Add labels for quantized vs fp16 vs fp32 runs; we had a regression previously when a quantized kernel was chosen unexpectedly. Also include which kernel selection policy was used (latency/cost/compat).

alex: noted. I'll open infra ticket with a rough dashboard mock and link to storage policy + CI PR.

maya: one more: add a small smoke test that asserts trace-quant can parse the uploaded file and produce expected json keys (kernel_name, total_time_ms, calls). That will catch upload format regressions.

alex: agreed, adding to PR. Thanks everyone — will post PR link when ready.
